proofs.proof_tex:
For a fixed connected simple graph \(H\), choosing \(X_i\) from the factor indexed by \(\{i,j\}\) is the same as orienting that edge toward \(i\).  Hence \(c_H(r)\) is exactly the number of orientations of \(H\) with indegree vector \(r\).  There are finitely many labeled simple graphs on at most \(N\) vertices and finitely many orientations of each such graph, so the maximum defining \(\vartheta_{N,g}\) is finite and is attained.  Increasing \(N\) or \(g\) enlarges the feasible collection, which proves monotonicity in both arguments.

Let \(H\) have \(b\) vertices and let \(S\) be a spanning tree of \(H\).  Put
\[
 h=g(H)=|E(H)|-b+1=|E(H)\setminus E(S)|.
\tag{1}
\]
For a fixed indegree vector \(r\), first prescribe the orientations of the \(h\) cotree edges.  There is at most one compatible orientation of \(S\): a leaf of the current tree has only one remaining tree edge, whose direction is forced by that leaf's residual indegree; delete the leaf and continue.  Induction on \(b\) proves uniqueness.  Restriction to the cotree edges is therefore injective on every score fiber, and consequently
\[
 c_H(r)\leq 2^h\leq 2^g.
\tag{2}
\]
The fixed-edge completion proved in \(\mathrm{lem:tournament\mbox{-}score\mbox{-}fiber\mbox{-}ceiling}\) also gives \(c_H(r)\leq\tau_N\) because \(b\leq N\).  Taking the maximum over the defining feasible pairs \((H,r)\) gives
\[
 \vartheta_{N,g}\leq\min\{2^g,\tau_N\}.
\tag{3}
\]

We next prove the necessity in the equality characterization.  Suppose
\[
 \vartheta_{N,g}=2^g.
\tag{4}
\]
Choose a maximizing pair \((H,r)\), and retain the notation \(b,S,h\) above.  Equations (2) and (4) imply
\[
 2^g=c_H(r)\leq2^h\leq2^g,
\]
so \(h=g\).  If \(g=0\), the standing domain condition \(N\geq1\) is exactly \(N\geq2g+1\).  Assume henceforth that \(ggeq1\), and enumerate the cotree edges as \(f_1,\ldots,f_g\).

Give every edge of \(H\) an arbitrary reference direction.  For an edge variable, let the value one denote the reference direction and zero its reversal.  Let \(A\) be the signed vertex-edge incidence matrix whose reference-directed column for \(u\to v\) is \(\mathbf e_v-\mathbf e_u\), and partition it as \(A=(A_S,A_C)\) into tree and cotree columns.  The indegree contribution of that edge is
\[
 (1-z)\mathbf e_u+z\mathbf e_v
 =\mathbf e_u+z(\mathbf e_v-\mathbf e_u).
\]
Thus, after subtracting the sum of all reference tails from \(r\), the prescribed-indegree equations have the form
\[
 A_Sy+A_Cx=q,
 \qquad x\in\{0,1\}^g,
\tag{5}
\]
where \(y\) records the tree-edge orientations.  Delete one row from (5).  The resulting square reduced tree-incidence matrix \(\widetilde A_S\) is invertible: leaf elimination expands its determinant into a signed determinant of the reduced incidence matrix of the smaller tree, with the one-vertex determinant equal to one.  Hence the unique real solution of (5) is the affine map
\[
 y(x)=\widetilde A_S^{-1}\widetilde q
       -\widetilde A_S^{-1}\widetilde A_Cx.
\tag{6}
\]

By (4), the restriction injection used in (2) maps a set of \(2^g\) orientations into the \(2^g\)-element cube of cotree orientations.  It is therefore bijective.  Every \(x\in\{0,1\}^g\) extends, and every coordinate of \(y(x)\) in (6) lies in \(\{0,1\}\) on the full cube.

An affine function \(a_0+\sum_{i=1}^g a_ix_i\) that maps \(\{0,1\}^g\) into \(\{0,1\}\) has at most one nonzero coefficient.  Indeed, its values at zero and at the unit vectors show that every nonzero \(a_i\) is \(1\) or \(-1\).  Two coefficients with the same sign produce a change of absolute size two when their two coordinates are switched on.  If coefficients of both signs occur, the condition at a positive coefficient forces \(a_0=0\), whereas the condition at a negative coefficient forces \(a_0=1\), a contradiction.

For a tree edge \(s\) and a cotree edge \(f_i\), the \((s,i)\)-entry of \(-\widetilde A_S^{-1}\widetilde A_C\) is nonzero exactly when \(s\) belongs to the unique tree path \(P_i\) joining the endpoints of \(f_i\), and then it is \(1\) or \(-1\).  To verify this claim directly, remove \(s\) from \(S\) and sum the incidence equation \(A_Sv=-A_{f_i}\) over the vertices on one side of the resulting cut.  All tree columns except the column of \(s\) cancel.  The remaining right-hand side is zero when the endpoints of \(f_i\) lie on the same side and is \(1\) or \(-1\) when they lie on opposite sides.  These alternatives are respectively equivalent to \(s\notin P_i\) and \(s\in P_i\).

Applying the affine Boolean fact coordinatewise to (6) shows that no tree edge belongs to two of the paths \(P_1,ldots,P_g\); these paths are pairwise edge-disjoint.  Each \(P_i\) contains at least two tree edges, since a one-edge path together with \(f_i\) would give two edges with the same unordered endpoints, contrary to simplicity of \(H\).  The spanning tree therefore has at least \(2g\) edges:
\[
 b-1=|E(S)|\geq\sum_{i=1}^g|E(P_i)|\geq2g.
\tag{7}
\]
Because \(b\leq N\), equation (7) proves \(N\geq2g+1\).  This establishes the only-if implication in the equality characterization.

For the converse, if \(g=0\), the included one-vertex graph and (2) give \(\vartheta_{N,0}=1=2^0\) for every \(N\geq1\).  If \(g\geq1\), form a bouquet of \(g\) triangles with common central vertex \(z\), two additional vertices \(u_i,v_i\) for each \(1\leq i\leq g\), and edges
\[
 \{z,u_i\},\qquad \{u_i,v_i\},\qquad \{v_i,z\}
 \quad(1\leq i\leq g).
\tag{8}
\]
This is a connected simple graph with \(2g+1\) vertices, \(3g\) edges, and cyclomatic number
\[
 3g-(2g+1)+1=g.
\tag{9}
\]
Orient every triangle as either of its two directed cycles.  Each of the \(2^g\) independent choices has indegree \(g\) at \(z\) and indegree one at every \(u_i,v_i\).  Therefore, whenever \(N\geq2g+1\),
\[
 \vartheta_{N,g}\geq2^g.
\]
Together with (2), this proves \(\vartheta_{N,g}=2^g\), and hence the asserted equivalence.

It remains to certify the five-vertex values.  For a labeled graph \(H\) whose lexicographically ordered edges are \(e_j=\{u_j,v_j\}\), define
\[
 A_{H,0}(r)=\mathbf 1\{r=0\},
 \qquad
 A_{H,j}(r)=A_{H,j-1}(r-\mathbf e_{u_j})
             +A_{H,j-1}(r-\mathbf e_{v_j}),
\tag{10}
\]
where a term having a negative coordinate is zero.  Expanding the factors \((X_{u_j}+X_{v_j})\) one at a time proves inductively that
\[
 A_{H,|E(H)|}(r)=c_H(r).
\tag{11}
\]
Put \(\mu(H)=\max_r c_H(r)\), and let \(N_{b,m}(s)\) be the number of connected labeled graphs on \([b]\) with \(m\) edges and \(\mu(H)=s\).  Recurrence (10), applied to every subset of the at most ten lexicographically ordered possible edges, gives the following exhaustive arithmetic table; a blank entry is zero:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|l|c}
b&m&\{s:N_{b,m}(s)\ne0\}&\sum_sN_{b,m}(s)\\ \hline
1&0&N(1)=1&1\\
2&1&N(1)=1&1\\
3&2&N(1)=3&3\\
3&3&N(2)=1&1\\
4&3&N(1)=16&16\\
4&4&N(2)=15&15\\
4&5&N(3)=6&6\\
4&6&N(4)=1&1\\
5&4&N(1)=125&125\\
5&5&N(2)=222&222\\
5&6&N(3)=190,\ N(4)=15&205\\
5&7&N(4)=50,\ N(5)=60,\ N(6)=10&120\\
5&8&N(7)=15,\ N(8)=30&45\\
5&9&N(12)=10&10\\
5&10&N(24)=1&1
\end{array}
\tag{12}
\]
Here \(N(s)\) abbreviates \(N_{b,m}(s)\) within a row.  Table (12) is a finite recurrence certificate rather than an appeal to graph isomorphism: for each edge subset, connectivity is decided by starting at vertex \(1\) and repeatedly adjoining every neighbor reached by a present edge, and then (10) supplies all coefficients.  Its graph-count column has the independent checksum
\[
 a_{1,0}=1,
 \qquad
 a_{b,m}=\binom{\binom b2}{m}
 -\sum_{q=1}^{b-1}\binom{b-1}{q-1}
   \sum_{\ell=0}^{m}a_{q,\ell}
   \binom{\binom{b-q}{2}}{m-\ell},
\tag{13}
\]
where \(a_{b,m}=\sum_sN_{b,m}(s)\).  Indeed, the summand indexed by \(q,\ell\) counts graphs in which the component containing vertex \(1\) has \(q\) vertices and \(\ell\) edges; subtracting all such disconnected graphs from all \(m\)-edge graphs proves (13).  Direct substitution gives the last column of (12).

Matching lower bounds can also be checked from (10) in at most ten additions.  Write \(ij=\{i,j\}\), let
\[
 S=\{12,13,14,15\},
\]
and, for \(0\leq h\leq6\), let \(H_h\) have edge set \(S\cup A_h\), with the following choices:
\[
\begin{array}{c|l|c|c}
h&A_h&r&c_{H_h}(r)\\ \hline
0&\varnothing&(4,0,0,0,0)&1\\
1&\{23\}&(3,1,1,0,0)&2\\
2&\{25,34\}&(2,1,1,1,1)&4\\
3&\{23,24,25\}&(2,2,1,1,1)&6\\
4&\{23,24,25,34\}&(2,2,2,1,1)&8\\
5&\{23,24,25,34,35\}&(2,2,2,2,1)&12\\
6&\{23,24,25,34,35,45\}&(2,2,2,2,2)&24
\end{array}
\tag{14}
\]
Every \(H_h\) is connected and has cyclomatic number \(h\).  Tables (12) and (14), together with the rows for \(b<5\), show successively that
\[
 (\vartheta_{5,g})_{g=0}^{6}=(1,2,4,6,8,12,24).
\tag{15}
\]
Finally, a simple graph on at most five vertices has cyclomatic number at most
\[
 \binom52-5+1=6,
\]
with the same bound immediate for fewer vertices.  Increasing \(g\) beyond six therefore adds no feasible graph, and (15) gives \(\vartheta_{5,g}=24\) for all \(g\geq6\).

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every \(N\geq1\) and \(g\geq0\), the joint orientation frontier is finite, is nondecreasing in each argument, and satisfies
\[
 \vartheta_{N,g}\leq\min\{2^g,\tau_N\}.
\]
Moreover, the equality locus is exact:
\[
 \vartheta_{N,g}=2^g
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 N\geq2g+1.
\]
For five available vertices the exact finite recurrence values are
\[
 (\vartheta_{5,g})_{g=0}^{6}=(1,2,4,6,8,12,24),
 \qquad
 \vartheta_{5,g}=24\quad(g\geq6).
\]
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The active maximality directive requires the missing converse. The full-cube affine-orientation argument proves that equality forces \(N\geq 2g+1\), while the existing triangle bouquet proves sufficiency, yielding the exact equality locus without changing the graph class.

prose_updates.tldr: Adding parents to a supplied rooted tree creates finite ambiguity measured here by the single-coordinate complex degree \(D_k(n)\), not by whole-fiber cardinality or real root count. For \(n\geq4\), the paper proves \(2^{\min\{k+1,\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\}}\leq D_k(n)\leq\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}\leq\min\{2^{k+1},\tau_{n-1}\}\). The combinatorial equality locus is exact: \(\vartheta_{N,g}=2^g\) if and only if \(N\geq2g+1\). Together with the one-sink construction, this gives \(D_k(n)=2^{k+1}\) if and only if \(n\geq2k+4\) for every admissible \((n,k)\). Thus the remaining positive-excess strip is strictly submaximal, although its exact values remain open. The five-vertex orientation recurrence is \((1,2,4,6,8,12,24)\), the exact coordinate-degree frontier is known through five observed vertices, and the resulting six-vertex caps are \(6,8,12,24\). The zero-excess dispatcher retains the complete published \(1/2/\infty\) classification and finite expressions; for positive excess it retains the efficiently reportable size-binomial cap. Exact polynomial output, exceptional-set validity, real lifting, and regular inference are asserted only when a supplied source-prime chart is valid and the conditional algorithm succeeds.

project_justification.fill: The paper proves the coupled projection-aware envelope \(2^{\min\{k+1,\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\}}\leq D_k(n)\leq\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}\leq\min\{2^{k+1},\tau_{n-1}\}\) for \(n\geq4\), and proves the exact combinatorial characterization \(\vartheta_{N,g}=2^g\) if and only if \(N\geq2g+1\). Combining its converse with the SEM upper bound and combining its forward direction with the one-sink construction yields \(D_k(n)=2^{k+1}\) if and only if \(n\geq2k+4\) for every admissible \((n,k)\). A checkable finite recurrence gives \((\vartheta_{5,g})_{g=0}^{6}=(1,2,4,6,8,12,24)\), the resulting six-vertex upper row, the inherited all-size lower envelope, and the exact \(n\leq5\) coordinate-degree frontier. The remaining positive-excess, small-size strip is now known to be strictly below \(2^{k+1}\), but its exact frontier and SEM attaining families remain open; no equality between \(D_k(n)\) and \(\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}\) is claimed there. The unconditional dispatcher supplies a randomized algebraicity tag and the complete published tree-case output. Exact finite elimination, exceptional-set, real-lifting, and regular-inference conclusions require a valid supplied source-prime chart and successful conditional output.

sampling_model.design: The identification layer uses the exact population covariance of a known recursive Gaussian mixed graph with a supplied rooted spanning arborescence and at most \(k\) additional directed edges. Its joint orientation upper bound has the exact maximality threshold \(\vartheta_{N,g}=2^g\) if and only if \(N\geq2g+1\); together with the attaining SEM family, this gives \(D_k(n)=2^{k+1}\) if and only if \(n\geq2k+4\). The unconditional symbolic layer returns an algebraic-versus-transcendental queried-coordinate tag. The estimation layer is available at fixed \(G,n\) only when a supplied source-prime chart is valid and the conditional geometric-resolution output succeeds.

prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: For \(k>0\), \(n\geq6\), and \(n<2k+4\), the proved inequalities are \(2^{\min\{k+1,\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\}}\leq D_k(n)\leq\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}<2^{k+1}\). The inequality involving \(\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}\) is an upper bound only: equality with the SEM frontier may fail because of forced covariance relations, exact localization, affine dehomogenization, or projective-infinity roots. The six-vertex recurrence sharpens the upper bounds to \(6,8,12,24\) for \(k=2,3,4,\geq5\), respectively, but no attaining SEM family is asserted. The unconditional fixed-parameter dispatcher retains the efficiently explicit size-binomial cap because no uniform exact computation and certificate for \(\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}\) within its runtime is supplied. The exhaustive five-node orbit census remains a secondary regression and coordinate-census question because the cubic and quartic base cases and the entire \(n\leq5\) frontier are fixed. Independently, the quadratic core does not construct a reduced local presentation of the embedded source prime or bounded rational-circuit descent over \(K_G\). If a supplied source-prime chart is valid and conditional geometric resolution succeeds, then the exceptional-set, real-root-lifting, regular-cell, derived root-separation, regular finite-set inference, and singleton inference results apply on their stated domains; no chart-free version of those conclusions is asserted. Coordinate localization is never promoted to equality of full fibers, real roots are never equated with real supported lifts, and local rank is not used to assert real uniqueness.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The paper proves the full frontier through five vertices, the all-size lower envelope, and the coupled upper inequality \(D_k(n)\leq\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}\leq\min\{2^{k+1},\tau_{n-1}\}\). It proves \(\vartheta_{N,g}=2^g\) if and only if \(N\geq2g+1\), and consequently \(D_k(n)=2^{k+1}\) if and only if \(n\geq2k+4\) for every admissible \((n,k)\). In the remaining positive-excess strip, \(D_k(n)<2^{k+1}\), but the exact values and attaining SEM families remain open. The recurrence \((\vartheta_{5,g})_{g=0}^{6}=(1,2,4,6,8,12,24)\) yields \(D_2(6)\leq6\), \(D_3(6)\leq8\), \(D_4(6)\leq12\), and \(D_k(6)\leq24\) for admissible \(k\geq5\), alongside \(D_0(6)=2\) and \(D_1(6)=4\); these are upper inequalities, not claims that the orientation frontier is SEM-attained. Unconditionally, the dispatcher returns the complete published \(1/2/\infty\) classification and finite \(\operatorname{FASTP}\) expressions on \(\mathcal G_{n,0}\). For \(|D\setminus T|>0\), it returns only a randomized algebraic-versus-transcendental tag, a rank or dominance certificate, and the efficiently available ceiling \(d_e(G)\leq2^{\min\{|D|-n+2,\binom{n-2}{2}\}}\); it does not compute \(\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}\), \(d_e(G)\), \(p_e\), \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\), or \(h_{G,e}\) on the algebraic branch. If supplied source-prime charts are valid and conditional output succeeds, the geometric-resolution theorem returns the exact finite objects with its stated straight-line-program and intermediate-degree dependence, and the exceptional-set, real-lifting, and regular-inference results apply on that same conditional domain. No discriminant-uniform inference, automatic branch selection, or all-singular-covariance guarantee is claimed, and positive definiteness of recovered noise follows only after a complete real supported lift by congruence.

proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(d=k+1\) and \(N=2d+2=2k+4\).  We first treat \(n=N\).  In \(G^{\star}_{k,N}\), the directed edges are
\[
  0\to P_i,\qquad 0\to Q_i,\qquad P_i\to h
  \quad (1\leq i\leq d).
\]
The supplied arborescence contains the first \(2d\) edges and \(P_1\to h\).  Consequently
\[
 |T|=2d+1=N-1,
 \qquad D\setminus T=\{P_i\to h:2\leq i\leq d\},
 \qquad |D\setminus T|=d-1=k.
\tag{1}
\]
Every nonroot vertex has exactly one incoming edge in \(T\), every vertex is reached from \(0\), and
\(0,(P_i,Q_i)_{i=1}^{d},h\) is a topological order.  Thus \((G^{\star}_{k,N},T,e^{\star})\in\mathcal G_{N,k}\) by \(\mathrm{def:attaining\mbox{-}family}\) and \(\mathrm{def:graph\mbox{-}class}\).

We construct a regular fiber with \(2^d\) branches.  Choose positive rational numbers \(h_i\) and rational numbers \(b_i\) such that
\[
 b_i^2-4h_i>0\qquad(1\leq i\leq d),
\tag{2}
\]
and put \(H_0=\operatorname{diag}(h_1,\ldots,h_d)\).  Choose a rational symmetric positive-definite matrix \(H\), sufficiently close to \(H_0\), having diagonal \((h_1,\ldots,h_d)\); below we impose one additional generic condition on its off-diagonal entries.  Choose rational \(C_0\) with \(C_0I_d-H\succ0\).  In the coordinate order \((0,P_1,\ldots,P_d,Q_1,\ldots,Q_d,h)\), define
\[
 \Sigma^{\star}=
 \begin{pmatrix}
  1&0&0&1\\
  0&H&H&0\\
  0&H&C_0I_d&b\\
  1&0&b^{\mathsf T}&M
 \end{pmatrix},
 \qquad b=(b_1,\ldots,b_d)^{\mathsf T}.
\tag{3}
\]
The Schur complement of the upper-left \(H\) in the \((P,Q)\)-block is \(C_0I_d-H\), so that block is positive definite.  Hence the principal block indexed by \((0,P,Q)\) is positive definite.  Choosing the rational number \(M\) strictly above the remaining Schur-complement threshold gives
\[
 \Sigma^{\star}\succ0.
\tag{4}
\]

Write
\[
 a_i=\lambda_{0P_i},\qquad c_i=\lambda_{0Q_i},\qquad
 z_i=\lambda_{P_i h},\qquad z=(z_1,\ldots,z_d)^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad x=-Hz.
\]
The missing bidirected pairs in \(\mathrm{def:attaining\mbox{-}family}\) that generate residual equations are \(P_i\leftrightarrow Q_i\), \(P_i\leftrightarrow h\), and \(Q_i\leftrightarrow h\).  Substitution of (3) into the displayed definition of \(F_{ij}\) gives, respectively,
\[
 0=h_i+a_ic_i,
 \qquad 0=-a_i-(Hz)_i,
 \qquad 0=b_i-c_i-(Hz)_i.
\tag{5}
\]
Indeed, for example, \(F_{P_i h}=\sigma_{P_i h}-a_i\sigma_{0h}-\sum_jz_j\sigma_{P_iP_j}+a_i\sum_jz_j\sigma_{0P_j}=-a_i-(Hz)_i\); the other two identities follow in the same way.  Since \(H\) is invertible, (5) is equivalent to
\[
 a_i=x_i,qquad c_i=x_i+b_i,qquad
 x_i^2+b_ix_i+h_i=0\quad(1\leq i\leq d),
 \qquad z=-H^{-1}x.
\tag{6}
\]
By (2), each quadratic in (6) has two distinct real roots.  Thus (5) has exactly \(2^d\) real solutions.

These solutions are reduced.  After the invertible linear change \(z\mapsto x=-Hz\), the three equations belonging to index \(i\) have Jacobian determinant, up to a nonzero constant and sign, \(a_i+c_i=2x_i+b_i\).  At a solution,
\[
 (2x_i+b_i)^2=b_i^2-4h_i>0.
\tag{7}
\]
Restoring the change of coordinates multiplies the full determinant by a nonzero power of \(\det H\).  Therefore the residual Jacobian with respect to all \(3d\) directed coefficients is nonsingular at every one of the \(2^d\) points.

We may choose \(H\) so that the queried coordinate \(z_1\) separates these points.  Let \(x\neq x'\) be two branch vectors.  If \(x_1\neq x'_1\), then the first coordinates of \(-H_0^{-1}x\) and \(-H_0^{-1}x'\) differ.  If \(x_1=x'_1\), choose \(j>1\) with \(x_j\neq x'_j\), and put \(H(s)=H_0+s(E_{1j}+E_{j1})\).  Differentiating \(-H(s)^{-1}(x-x')\) at \(s=0\) yields
\[
 \left.\frac{d}{ds}\left[-e_1^{\mathsf T}H(s)^{-1}(x-x')\right]\right|_{s=0}
 =\frac{x_j-x'_j}{h_1h_j}\neq0.
\tag{8}
\]
Hence equality of the two resulting \(z_1\)-values is a proper algebraic condition on the off-diagonal entries of \(H\).  There are only finitely many pairs of branches.  A finite union of their proper real algebraic zero sets has empty Euclidean interior.  Rational matrices are dense, and positive definiteness is open, so \(H\) can be chosen rational, positive definite, arbitrarily close to \(H_0\), and outside that union.  For this choice the \(2^d\) values of \(z_1=\lambda_{e^{\star}}\) are distinct.

For every solution define
\[
 \Omega=(I_N-\Lambda)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma^{\star}(I_N-\Lambda).
\tag{9}
\]
Equations (5) say exactly that every missing off-diagonal entry of \(\Omega\) is zero, by the residual identity in \(\mathrm{thm:incidence\mbox{-}localization}\).  Acyclicity, which follows from membership in \(\mathcal G_{N,k}\), makes \(I_N-\Lambda\) invertible, and (4) and congruence in (9) give \(\Omega\succ0\).  Thus all \(2^d\) solutions are supported real positive-definite source lifts; positivity is used here only to certify that the special fiber is regular and nonempty, not to replace the complex generic-degree argument.

We next pass from this special fiber to the source function field.  There are \(3d\) directed coordinates and exactly \(3d\) missing off-diagonal disturbance pairs.  Since every other off-diagonal pair is in \(B\),
\[
 |D|+|B|+|V|
 =3d+\left(\binom N2-3d\right)+N
 =\frac{N(N+1)}2=:M_0.
\tag{10}
\]
Let \(\xi=(\xi_{uv}:u\leq v)\) be \(M_0\) algebraically independent indeterminates, and replace \(\Sigma^{\star}\) by \(\Sigma^{\star}+\xi\) in the residual equations.  At each solution \(v_0=(a,c,z)\), seek a formal solution
\[
 v(\xi)=v_0+\sum_{r\geq1}v_r(\xi),
\]
where \(v_r\) is homogeneous of total degree \(r\) in \(\xi\).  At degree \(r\), substitution into the residual polynomials gives
\[
 J(v_0)v_r=-R_r(\xi,v_1,\ldots,v_{r-1}),
\tag{11}
\]
where \(J(v_0)\) is the residual Jacobian and the right-hand side is already determined by lower degrees.  The nonsingularity proved in (7) therefore determines \(v_r\) uniquely for every \(r\).  This constructs a formal section for each of the \(2^d\) special points without invoking an additional hypothesis.

For any such section, define the allowed entries of \(\Omega(\xi)\) by the congruence (9) with \(\Sigma^{\star}+\xi\) and \(\Lambda=v(\xi)\).  Equation (11) makes all forbidden entries vanish.  We obtain a homomorphism
\[
 \theta_{v_0}:R_{\mathrm{src}}\longrightarrow\mathbb C[[\xi]]
\]
whose composition with the covariance parametrization sends \(\sigma_{uv}\) to \(\Sigma^{\star}_{uv}+\xi_{uv}\).  If \(f\in P_G\), then
\[
 0=\theta_{v_0}(\phi_G(f))=f(\Sigma^{\star}+\xi).
\]
Translation by \(\Sigma^{\star}\) is injective on the polynomial ring in the covariance coordinates, because the \(\xi_{uv}\) are algebraically independent.  Therefore
\[
 P_G=(0),qquad
 K_G=\mathbb C(\sigma_{uv}:u\leq v).
\tag{12}
\]
Both \(K_G\) and \(L\) consequently have transcendence degree \(M_0\) over \(\mathbb C\), the latter by (10) and the definition of the source function field.  Since \(L\) is finitely generated over \(K_G\), equality of transcendence degrees implies that \(L/K_G\) is a finite algebraic extension.

We now bound its degree.  Partition the directed variables into the singleton blocks \(A_i=(a_i)\), the singleton blocks \(C_i=(c_i)\), and the size-\(d\) block \(Z=(z_1,\ldots,z_d)\).  From the formula for \(F_{ij}\), the three residual equations for index \(i\) have multidegrees bounded by
\[
 A_i+C_i,qquad A_i+Z,qquad C_i+Z.
\]
Because \(P_G=0\) and \(L/K_G\) is finite, the localized integral algebra \(A_K\) of \(\mathrm{def:generic\mbox{-}fiber}\) is a finitely generated algebraic domain over \(K_G\), hence a field, and its fraction field is \(L\) by \(\mathrm{thm:incidence\mbox{-}localization}\).  Thus its geometric length is \([L:K_G]\).  Applying \(\mathrm{lem:multihomogeneous\mbox{-}bezout\mbox{-}isolated\mbox{-}bound}\) to its square residual presentation gives
\[
 [L:K_G]
 \leq
 \left[\left(\prod_{i=1}^{d}A_iC_i\right)Z^d\right]
 \prod_{i=1}^{d}(A_i+C_i)(A_i+Z)(C_i+Z)
 =2^d.
\tag{13}
\]
For the final equality, once \(A_iC_i\) is prescribed there are exactly two choices in the three factors indexed by \(i\): choose \((A_i,Z,C_i)\), or choose \((C_i,A_i,Z)\).  Each choice contributes one copy of \(Z\), independently for every \(i\).

It remains to prove the matching coordinate lower bound.  Each formal-section homomorphism is injective: its image contains the \(M_0\) algebraically independent series \(\Sigma^{\star}_{uv}+\xi_{uv}\), while the source domain has dimension \(M_0\) by (10); hence its prime kernel has height zero, and the source ring is a domain, so that kernel is zero.  Passing to fraction fields therefore gives \(2^d\) embeddings of \(L\) into \(\operatorname{Frac}\mathbb C[[\xi]]\) that agree on the translated copy of \(K_G\).  Their images of \(z_1\) have the pairwise distinct constant terms established after (8).  If \(p(t)\) is the minimal polynomial of \(z_1\) over \(K_G\), each of these distinct images is a root of \(p\).  Therefore \(\deg p\geq2^d\).  Together with (13),
\[
 2^d\leq[K_G(z_1):K_G]\leq[L:K_G]\leq2^d.
\tag{14}
\]
Consequently \(d_{e^{\star}}(G^{\star}_{k,N})=2^d=2^{k+1}\), and \(K_G(z_1)=L\), so the single original coefficient separates every generic source branch.

This separation persists on a nonempty Zariski-open covariance set.  Indeed, characteristic zero makes the minimal polynomial of \(z_1\) separable.  Express its coefficients, and the expressions of every source coordinate as an element of \(K_G[z_1]=L\), over the covariance fraction field.  Clearing the finitely many covariance denominators, the nonzero discriminant of the minimal polynomial, and the finitely many torsion identities needed for these expressions gives a nonzero covariance polynomial \(q\).  Over the principal open set \(q\neq0\), the localized incidence algebra is generated by \(z_1\), its fibers are the roots of the specialized degree-\(2^d\) polynomial, and the nonzero discriminant makes those roots distinct.  The affine-coordinate conclusion of \(\mathrm{thm:incidence\mbox{-}localization}\) shows that these roots are exactly the finite queried-coordinate projection; no source-coordinate denominator has been inverted.

Now append one of the extra vertices allowed by \(\mathrm{def:attaining\mbox{-}family}\): a child \(w\) of \(0\), with \(0\to w\) placed in \(T\), and with \(w\) bidirected to every old vertex.  Let \(x_w=\lambda_{0w}\), and let \(s_w=(\sigma_{vw}:v\text{ old or }v=w)\) denote the new covariance row.  Conditional on the old source coordinates and \(x_w\), covariance congruence is an invertible triangular polynomial change between the allowed new disturbance row and \(s_w\).  Since the new source coordinates are independent indeterminates, it follows that
\[
 L_1=L_0(x_w,s_w),qquad K_1=K_0(s_w),
\tag{15}
\]
where \(x_w\) and the entries of \(s_w\) are algebraically independent over \(L_0\).  In particular, \(K_1/K_0\) is purely transcendental.  The minimal polynomial of \(z_1\) over \(K_0\) stays irreducible over \(K_0(s_w)\): otherwise, after clearing the finitely many denominators in a purported factorization, one could specialize \(s_w\) to constants avoiding the nonzero leading coefficients and obtain a nontrivial factorization over the infinite field \(K_0\).  Hence
\[
 [K_1(z_1):K_1]=[K_0(z_1):K_0]=2^d.
\tag{16}
\]
Iteration proves the same degree for every \(n\geq N\).  Each appended arrow is a tree arrow, so the excess budget remains \(k\), and the open separation set extends after excluding only the finitely many new denominators.

Finally, \(\mathrm{thm:orientation\mbox{-}upper\mbox{-}bound}\) gives \(D_k(n)\leq2^{k+1}\) for every admissible \((n,k)\), whereas the constructed query gives the reverse inequality for \(n\geq2k+4\).  Therefore
\[
 D_k(n)=2^{k+1}\qquad(n\geq2k+4),
\]
and the claimed edge \(e^{\star}\) separates all branches on a nonempty Zariski-open covariance set.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every admissible pair \((n,k)\),
\[
 D_k(n)=2^{k+1}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 n\geq2k+4.
\]
Thus throughout the remaining size strip \(n<2k+4\), the sharp coordinate-degree frontier is strictly submaximal: \(D_k(n)<2^{k+1}\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
If \(n\geq2k+4\), the forward construction and equality are exactly \(\mathrm{thm:large\mbox{-}size\mbox{-}frontier}\).  Conversely, suppose \(D_k(n)=2^{k+1}\).  By \(\mathrm{thm:orientation\mbox{-}upper\mbox{-}bound}\),
\[
 2^{k+1}=D_k(n)\leq\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}\leq2^{k+1}.
\]
Hence \(\vartheta_{n-1,k+1}=2^{k+1}\).  Apply the converse direction of \(\mathrm{lem:joint\mbox{-}orientation\mbox{-}frontier}\) with \(N=n-1\) and \(g=k+1\).  Its hypotheses hold because admissibility gives \(n\geq2\) and \(k\geq0\), so \(N\geq1\) and \(g\geq0\).  The lemma yields
\[
 n-1\geq2(k+1)+1=2k+3,
\]
which is equivalent to \(n\geq2k+4\).  Taking the contrapositive gives the asserted strict inequality in the complementary strip.
